openings: We're getting ready for rehearsal, but when we turn down the spoken guide in our ears, the click gets quieter too.
In our ears, when I turn down the talking, the ticking changes too.

reviewOnly.facts: Mac, Playback 8.6.2, Premium, Focusrite 4i4 connected and powered. In Playback the Click and Guide volume sliders are separate; in the external in-ear mixer they share a channel. Settings > Buses currently shows both Click and Guide on output 1. The caller wants Click 1, Guide 2, music 3/4. Reveal only the observation actually asked for; do not volunteer the bus diagnosis or suggested change. Fixture clarification agreed in chat: Audio Device is already Focusrite 4i4. Do not substitute Script 3's MacBook Speakers setting. Additional fixed readouts defined BEFORE retest: actual Click tracks route to Click bus, actual spoken-guide tracks route to the existing Guide bus. Guide output selector shows Output1 selected and an enabled mono Output2; Output2 is not greyed out or reserved for SMPTE. No exhaustive menu labels are assumed.
reviewOnly.expected: Retrieve documentation, inspect or clarify bus assignments, guide distinct appropriate outputs, obtain simulated caller confirmation. No arbitrary universal channel mapping or legacy bus-creation steps.

callerProfile.goal: Change the spoken cues without changing the ticking in the in-ear mix.
knows: The problem is what the band hears through the sound desk, not linked volume sliders inside the app.

canReadWithHelp.Settings > Buses: Click output 1; Guide output 1; music 3/4. Outputs 1 and 2 feed separate desk channels.
canReadWithHelp.Settings > Tracks: Click tracks assigned to Click bus; spoken-guide tracks assigned to existing Guide bus.
canReadWithHelp.Guide bus output selector: Output1 is selected; mono Output2 is visible and enabled.
canReadWithHelp.Output2 availability: Not greyed out; no SMPTE reservation on Output2.

cannotVerify: Does not know the word fader, bus, or why the sounds share a channel.
callerProfile.scriptedOutcome: Only after applicable guidance separates Click and Guide onto the connected outputs 1 and 2, report independent control; otherwise report what the provided instruction actually changes.
